title: Full system freeze and resources exhaustion
body:
### Tested versions

- 100% Reproducible in: 4.7.1.stable.mono (Windows, x86_64), 4.6.3.stable.mono (Windows, x86_64)
- Not reproducible when the game window is not embedded, e.g. running stand-alone, non-embedded, via command line, etc.
- Reproduces on both Forward+/Vulkan and Forward+/D3D12 (multi-monitor)

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9571) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 63.72 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

With Game Embed Mode enabled, running a project from the editor (F5) intermittently takes the entire machine down: the desktop stops responding and only recovers when the game process is force-killed. Sometimes the game process instead dies on its own with `Program crashed with signal 11`.

Measurements taken while a frozen run was still alive:

|  |  |
|---|---|
| GPU VRAM | **15995 MiB of 16376 MiB** (exhausted) |
| Game process private bytes | 19 GB, working set 5 GB and climbing |
| CPU | kernel/GPU time pinned, DWM starved |
| Managed (C#) heap | flat at ~105 MB, unchanged throughout |
| Managed threads | all idle (worker threads parked in `Monitor.Wait`) |
| Main thread | `[Native Frames]` only - no managed frames at all |

So the runaway is engine/driver-side allocation, not application allocation: the process holds gigabytes of GPU memory that WDDM is spilling back into system memory, while the application itself is doing nothing.

When it crashes instead of hanging, the backtrace shows a native self-recursion whose depth varies between runs - the same frame repeats 7x in one run and 8x in the next, entered from an address 0x6b earlier in the same function:

```
Embedded window only supports Windowed mode.

================================================================
CrashHandlerException: Program crashed with signal 11
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.7.1.stable.mono.official (a13da4feb8d8aefc283c3763d33a2f170a18d541)
...
[10] 7ff70d1f5419 (main+2605419)
[11] 7ff70d1f53ae (main+26053ae)   <-- repeats 7-8 times, depth varies per run
[12] 7ff70d1f53ae (main+26053ae)
...
[18] 7ff70d3ce1c8 (main+27de1c8)
[19] 7ff70ea63a80 (main+3e73a80)
```

Every affected run logs `Embedded window only supports Windowed mode.` beforehand (the project asks for a maximized window at startup, which an embedded window refuses).

**Workaround:** Editor Settings -> Run -> Window Placement -> Game Embed Mode = Disabled (`run/window_placement/game_embed_mode = -1`). With embedding off the same project runs indefinitely with no freeze.

Possibly relevant configuration at repro time:
- `run/window_placement/game_embed_mode = 0`, `run/window_placement/screen = -5` (same as Editor)
- `.godot/editor/project_metadata.cfg` -> `[game_view] embed_size_mode = 2` (Stretch - the Game dock resizes the embedded window continuously)
- The editor sat on a monitor at x >= 3840, and launched the game with `--position "3910,540" --resolution 1920x1080 --wid <hwnd>`

#### What does not reproduce it

Running the game from a shell with the editor's own command line, including `--wid` embedding into a host window, `--remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:6007` with a listener accepting, and the same off-screen `--position "3910,540"`, ran clean for 60 s:

```
Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64.exe --path <project> --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:6007 \
  --editor-pid <pid> --scene <uid> --wid <hwnd> --position "3910,540" --resolution 1920x1080
```

Plain standalone runs are also clean, including maximizing to 4K. The editor's live management of the embedded window therefore appears to be required, not merely the embedded window itself.

### Steps to reproduce

* Open the project
* F5 to run the game in the embedded viewer
* Maximize the window

After changing lots of settings and the Game Embed Mode to fix this, I am no longer able repro this again. However, the issue was 100% persistent and reproducible until the "workaround" was performed.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

When it was happening, I was able to repro with literally empty project/scene: [embed-freeze-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30868841/embed-freeze-mrp.zip)
